Senses.Note: One named-person sense covers Lü Dongbin, Lü Chunyang, and the True Person Pure Yang. Criticism of longevity and alchemy, positive sword portraiture, and changed conduct after meeting Huanglong are different recorded stances toward the same figure, not separate people or lexical senses. The encounter witnesses abbreviate the other figure to Huanglong. They do not name Huanglong Huinan or connect Lü to Huinan's later Three Barriers, so that former related-term link has been removed; the likely Huanglong Huiji identity remains a context question for the dedicated roster pass rather than a silently asserted link here.

Senses.Explanation: Minshu raises Lü Dongbin as the sword-bearing immortal who tries to strike Huanglong with a flying sword but is instead transformed and awakened by him; Minshu then quotes Lü abandoning his gourd and lute, no longer refining mercury into gold, and recognizing that his earlier effort was wasted after seeing Huanglong. Xisou Shaotan titles a verse ‘Lü Dongbin meets Huanglong,’ says that even long life finally decays, and describes Huanglong as covering or protecting Lü. Wuwen Daocan says that Lü walks freely only after personally seeing Huanglong. These three named speakers make Lü Huanglong's immortal visitor in this dictionary. Wumen Huikai's portrait names sword-bearing Lü Dongbin, has him bare the blade and wield commands of killing and giving life, and ends by naming him the True Person Pure Yang. At a formal installation, Yunshan Yanju Shen strikes his staff and says that he breaks Lü Dongbin's elixir cauldron to pieces. Qiaoyin Wuyi's portrait retains Lü's Daoist clothing, boxed sword, Penglai setting, and wine. These named raisers and portrait writers define the Zen figure through the Huanglong encounter and its later sword, longevity, cauldron, clothing, and changed-bearing scenes, not through an imported immortal's biography or a single inferred lesson.

Senses.Explanation: A watched fishing line can eclipse the reeds beside it. Jiqi and Xiaotang turn questions about an absent person toward the scene beside the line. Minshu and Yue'an use the pair to test attention to what a narrow search overlooks.

Senses.PreferredTarget: People see this single flower as though in a dream
AlternateTargets: People look at this one flower as if dreaming
SearchAliases: one flower seen as in a dream
seeing this flower as though dreaming
Senses.Note: The official Lu asks Nanquan about the claim that heaven, earth, and all beings share one root. Nanquan points to a peony in the courtyard and says that people see this one flower as though in a dream. Fushi, Yingshan, Eryin, Hanxiu, Luyan, and Danya each bring the old exchange into a new sermon, comment, or verse. The line tests whether a listener turns the flower into an idea or actually meets what Nanquan points out.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2008.xml). Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch. In this Platform Scripture account, Shenxiu worries about presenting his understanding and writes his verse secretly on the corridor wall: body as awakening tree, mind as bright mirror stand, constantly wiping it so dust does not gather. The Fifth Ancestor publicly commends practicing and reciting it, yet privately tells Shenxiu he remains outside the gate and has not seen his nature. The headword is Shenxiu's authored instruction within that reported episode. Its encouragement of continued clearing and the narrator's critical assessment must both remain visible; neither the public commendation nor the private rebuke alone gives the whole scene, and the text's presentation is not an independently witnessed transcript.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu quotes a critic who classes Shenxiu's wiping verse as practice clinging to existence and therefore an ordinary person's method. He rejects reducing Shenxiu to that judgment, invoking Nanyue's statement that practice and realization occur while contamination must not. Shenxiu's expression may be less rounded, he says, but cannot simply be called ordinary. He also attacks the critic's dismissal of Huineng's no-tree verse as an outsider's emptiness. The headword is Shenxiu's quoted verse inside a polemical defense; Tianyin qualifies its expression without treating the two verses as a simple wrong-versus-right diagram.

He says one elder cries injustice while holding stolen goods and the other mistakes a servant for the master: neither has shown awakening's precise matter. The current demonstration recasts both old formulations rather than endorsing either repeated polishing or its verbal negation as a sufficient final answer.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB442.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Daxiaochong. While speaking on discipline, Daxiao Xingchong first uses startling language about freedom from conventional prohibitions but immediately insists on vigilance like walking on thin ice. He retells Shenxiu and Huineng presenting their opposed verses, judges one to have a killing blade without a reviving sword and the other the reverse, and proposes thirty staff blows for each so later people will not cling to one side. What if someone said he too deserves thirty? He strikes the table and answers with Liu Yi carrying a message to Dongting Lake. The headword is Shenxiu's cited instruction; the whole turn resists both one-sided doctrinal verdicts and careless permission to abandon discipline.

Senses.Explanation: ‘When the time comes’ marks a fitting moment finally arriving. A master may say it as spring breaks through, as a student's long effort ripens, or as a warning that one must be ready before a crisis appears. Yinyuan Longqi uses spring arriving after long stagnant water to open a sermon and then challenges the audience to show a warrant. Zhe'an Jingfan says that when the time comes a lifelong resolve is fulfilled. At the Dragon Boat festival, Lianfeng Su tells the brothers not to miss this occasion. Pu'an Yinsu likens the arrival to waking from a dream after long cultivation. Guting Shanjian warns against copying old masters' gestures: with close sustained effort, a sudden break comes when its time arrives. At a New Year gathering, Tianran Hanshi says the moment has arrived without seeking and that what was always present is returned. In a written instruction Yuanwu Keqin warns that someone who waits until the last moment, like digging a well only when thirsty, cannot expect to be ready.

Senses.Note: “When the season arrives, its principle shows itself” is voiced amid different occasions. Jianguan points to rice shoots, wheat, and moonlight; Wuzhun raises his staff as a rain-bringing dragon; Shitian asks what the opening of summer retreat reveals. Senses.Explanation: To seek fire is the action in the repeatedly raised answer, “the fire-boy comes seeking fire.” Fayan Wenyi refuses Xuanze’s explanation that this simply means using fire to seek fire or using oneself to seek oneself; elsewhere masters pair seeking fire with striking or carving ice, making it an image of a search whose chosen means cannot yield what is sought. Qinglin Shiqian first answers Xuanze’s question about his own self with “the fire-boy comes seeking fire.” When Xuanze later explains the line to Fayan as fire seeking fire and self seeking self, Fayan says that understanding will not do. Fayan then has Xuanze ask the question again and gives the same answer himself. The repeated words therefore survive while Xuanze’s explanatory menu is expressly rejected. Feiyin Tongrong pairs “carving ice to seek fire” with “steaming sand to make rice.” The Questions Posed to the Chan School later classifies the fire-boy answer as a living phrase while recording the rejected fire-with-fire explanation. These are one lexical action, not separate senses: the fire-boy case, seeking fire with fire, and seeking it from ice vary the seeker and means while retaining the act of seeking fire.

Guting Shanjian warns against substituting memorized knowledge, fame or verbal skill for settling birth and death. A person who laughs off the difficulty can reach the crisis of dying unable either to gain life or to obtain death, like a living turtle shedding its shell or an ox being flayed. He urges continuous investigation of the word 'no,' then warns against holding even an experience as awakening; earlier confusion and later awakening must both disappear. The headword describes the feared crisis that motivates his exhortation. It is not an instruction to seek injury or death, and his promise of a later opening is part of this teaching address.

Senses.Explanation: Guting Shanjian warns against substituting memorized knowledge, fame or verbal skill for settling birth and death. A person who laughs off the difficulty can reach the crisis of dying unable either to gain life or to obtain death, like a living turtle shedding its shell or an ox being flayed. He urges continuous investigation of the word 'no,' then warns against holding even an experience as awakening; earlier confusion and later awakening must both disappear. ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ：我不會勘得儞，且點一椀茶與儞濕口。意在於何？路逢劒客須呈劒，不是詩人不獻詩。上堂，舉：馬大師道：羅漢聞見佛性，菩薩眼見佛性。了達無二，名平等性。師云：蔣山著一隻眼，要與馬大師相見去也。天神歸天，地神歸地，錢歸庫，馬歸槽。仰望虗空，伏惟珍重。便下座。行履畝法，上堂。山前一片閑田地，師云：物見主，眼卓竪。叉手叮嚀問祖翁，師云：自家本來契券何在？幾度賣來還自買。師云：磬聲斷後，不得翻悔。為憐松竹引清風。師云：利動君子。東山敗缺已被蔣山點破了也，且道蔣山敗缺還有人點撿也無？良久，云：我皇有勑，大赦咸放。上堂，舉：晦堂謂圓悟云：勤兄近日如何？悟云：起滅不停。晦堂云：可知博地凡夫，我二十年前也曾恁麼來，而今會也，脚尖頭也踢出一箇佛。師云：非起滅不停底博地凡夫，安能脚尖頭也踢出一箇佛？果然脚尖頭踢出一箇佛，始是箇起滅不停底博地凡夫。地靈步步雪山草，僧寶人人滄海珠。上堂：黃梅意旨，會佛法人不得。臨濟正眼，向這瞎驢邊滅。只此兩著，殃害天下衲僧。求生不得生，求死不得死。因思鐵觜老禪和解道，先師無此語。上堂，舉僧問石頭：如何是禪？頭云：碌磚。如何是道？頭云：木頭。師云：明水大羮，鮮能知味；匏土革木，罕遇知音。上堂：枯木龍吟，一切音響俱絕。髑髏眼活，一切色相皆空。覰著即瞎，聽著即聾。堪笑觀音大士，無端也證圓通。謝化士歸，上堂，舉：僧辤大隋，隋云：甚處去？僧云：下山教化去。隋云：盡大地是吾檀越，儞向甚處化？僧云：便請疏頭。隋云：儞去未得在。師云：大隋有射鵰之手，箭不虗施；這僧具嚙鏃之機，當鋒咬住。因甚麼大隋却道儞去未得在？良久，云：真金若不經爐鞴，爭得光華徹底鮮？上堂，舉：僧辤趙州，州云：甚處去？僧云：雪峯去。趙州云：若問和尚有何言句，儞作麼生祇對？僧云：却請和尚道。師云：這僧雖善倒轉鎗頭，未免鋒刃不利。州云：冬言寒，夏言熱。又問僧云：忽然問：畢竟事作麼生？僧無語。州云：但言親到趙州來，不是傳語漢。師云：總道趙州向這僧面前呈款，殊不知就中有吞併天下英雄之謀。僧後到雪峯，峯云：甚處來？僧云：趙州來。峯云：有何言句？僧舉前話，師云：傳言送語也未得在。峯云：須是趙州始得。師云：口甜心苦得人憎。復召大眾云：當時這僧若具未舉先知底眼目，二大老須向佗手中乞命。然雖如是，趙州關險人難透，雪嶠峯高路不通。上堂

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 道如何會？江南地煖，塞北春寒，越聖超凡句，目前無正偏，世尊纔拈起，飲光便破顏，亦似龍騰滄海、鳳渡長空，大千沙界一點塵，遍界無非是玅體，更說甚麼紅塵世內、清虛界外，明明赤手空拳，處處逍遙無礙，一切存亡向此透脫，本有家風，自然上契佛祖根源、下合眾生心地，所謂通玄峰頂，不是人間，心外無法，滿目青山。且道報恩一句作麼生道？仰望碧空空不見，無心回顧正當頭。」拍膝，下座。佛誕日，蓬邑生員楊大來請上堂。「黃面無端此日生，滿腔毒放太驚群，胡言漢語分高下，秪到於今成禍根。」以杖指空，云：「誰家不具超群智？個個眉毛眼上橫。李老君云：『大道廢，有仁義。』復一喝：太平本是將軍致，不許將軍見太平。」師誕日，上堂。「若道今日是生，月前湛無水之波。教云：『若取法相，即著我、人、眾生、壽者。』若道無生，劫外糝枯木之花。『若取非法相，即著我、人、眾生、壽者。』若道無生，即生生是無生。是故不應取法，不應取非法。法上應捨，何況非法。既作出家丈夫，豁開正眼，了了明明，求生不得生，求死不得死。此是古家風，本無陰陽萬象。其或未然，長年墮在講誦學解，永為外道種族。偈曰：不識何緣天地先，至尊無相至虛玄。非離非合非明暗，遍覆大千不露顏。」示眾，上堂。「禪道若用參學，污賤家珍反外彫錯。絕慮忘機達本，妄歇情消無著。若執無心無事人，何異聲聞執法縛？萬古碧潭空界月，再三撈摝始應知。」上堂開示。「學個大丈夫，不論僧俗男女，只遺達本，莫逐其末。達本人無為絕學，無事無住著，隨流得玅，無事於心、無心於事，世出世間無染礙，無事合融萬象空。逐末人學解多聞，生滅取舍，染靜修證，精進間斷，因果福田，種種分別，執法萬千，人我自高。將謂有佛可成，有禪可參，有道理可學，有眾生可度；將謂有家可歸，有生死去來；將謂有彼岸可登，別有佛國可居；將謂有陰陽萬象；將謂實有天堂地獄、四生六道，有法可傳；將謂有神通，福報是玄玅。善惡如浮雲，本體如太虛，佛說一大藏教，止啼黃葉、途路藥方。歷代祖師直指現前，人人具足，物外污染。今時人秪向途路藥方上尋討，任你數算到八萬劫後，墮在聲聞外道，於己無益。看來到江吳地盡，隔岸越山多。」上堂開示，問答不錄。「風和日暖，國泰民安，古佛家風，柳綠桃紅，滿眼玄玅，鳥蹄花笑，開正法眼，晝明夜暗，歷歷孤明，本無增減，春生夏長，秋收冬藏，無言

Occurrences.Kwic: 魚龍與蝦蠏，大身復有阿修羅。天台遠也侍吾久，出紙乞我西源歌。歌西源，無滴水。佛也祖也，徹頭徹尾。今兮古兮，透頂透底。更說甚麼竺乾震旦，南岳石頭，馬大師，龐居士。只因一口吸西江，無限波濤從此起。一源一源羣靈一源，假名為佛。佛既假名，源從何出？釋迦老子曾未悟，四十九年曲流布。誰言教外有別傳，百萬人天空罔措。先聖道：流泉是命，湛寂是身。從本不清不濁，即今非古非新。四大海收歸涓滴，五須彌卷入微塵。徧界金波常帀帀，與他凡聖無交涉。海屋海屋普門道人索我謌，未免平地生風波。屋為海耶海為屋，海屋之義當如何。百千瀛渤從此起，起亦不離涓滴水。沃日滔天也大奇，卷舒只在軒窻裡。我觀觀音心海空，一一佛屋羅其中。接影連輝寶樓閣，珠幢玉樹光玲瓏。及乎斂念元無有，試問道人知此否。不下禪牀徧十方，春風自裊金瓶柳。谷隱谷隱龍以角聽，蟻以身聽。人聽在耳，風鳴谷應。聽到無聲谷自空，山河石壁遙相通。直饒千手掩不得，所以八面俱玲瓏。雖然隱也何曾隱，白日青天雷輥輥。閒閒閒閒終日忙忙，那事無妨。行住坐臥，一絲不掛。看經費眼力，作福受奔波。饑來喫飯困來睡，如此閑閑快活何。佛日普照慧辯楚石禪師語錄卷第十七音切巘壜摩挲嵊湓栲栳奯陡荄崱屴鎌菅佛日普照慧辯楚石禪師語錄卷第十八偈頌四偈頌四侍者文斌等編明真頌二十八首明真頌二十八首我有摩尼一顆，埋在五蘊身田，昨向泥中取出，光明照燭無邊。所為莫不知意，日用尋常現前，世上誰無此寶？昏迷未脫葢纏。死生生死縈絆，果報或人或天，一旦逢善知識，豈非有大因緣？只這言語聲色，非根非塵非識。釋迦親見燃燈，故號能仁寂默。平治自家田地，淨除瓦礫荊棘。身光充徧十虗，豈止百千萬億。一念成佛不疑，多方轉化何極。雖云妙行莊嚴，畢竟歸無所得。觸目無非此道，莫揀精麤大小。眾生與佛何殊，總是自心所造。修善天堂化生，受用珍奇異寶。地獄皆由作惡，鐵牀銅柱圍繞。臨終罪業現前，方恨悔之不早。覺悟煩惱菩提，迷惑菩提煩惱。禪師不假多知，饑飡渴飲隨時，將心用心大錯，在道修道堪悲。內外推尋不見，中間亦絕毫釐，眾生別求智慧，諸佛何異愚癡？一等黃金作器，瓶盤釵釧環兒，自體元無改變，千般任用爐鎚。貪嗔癡號三毒，三毒起於一心。本來空寂三毒，三毒自此平沈。頓獲金剛正體，親聞大覺圓音。了然不生不滅，解者非古非今。智士現前究竟，愚人向外推尋。

Senses.PreferredTarget: Handling incense and fire all day, unaware that the body is the place of awakening
SearchAliases: handling incense and fire all day, unaware that the body is the place of awakening
Senses.Note: The line says one may handle incense and tend fire all day while failing to know that one’s own body is the place of awakening. Daxiu answers it with a verse about morning water and an old fire. Fangrong objects that the old version and Xuan Sha’s revised version can both become another shrine to seek. Hongzhi mocks such spiritual searching. Shenfeng tests three related formulations; Hansong refuses even to name the action as tending incense and fire, and Pinjixiang dismisses the group as making mud balls. These responses keep the saying from becoming a claim that ritual objects or the body alone settle the matter.
